verdicts.reason: A keeps a sensible order (logo, headline, copy, bags, CTA) with a large CTA at the bottom. But the flavour names are stacked apart from their descriptors and in a different order, so they no longer match. One giant bag sits beside two tiny ones, and the text block is jammed. B has the same broken flavour list plus worse problems: a tiny CTA crammed into the top-left corner like a badge, illegibly squeezed body copy, and two mini bags dumped against the bottom-left edge with dead space beside them.

A leads with the bag, a reasonably sized headline and a strong CTA. However, the Solstice logo is buried as a speck at the very bottom, the flavour names and descriptors are split and mismatched, and the mini bags are pushed off-axis to the left. B (the same layout as pair 1 B) has a buried tiny CTA at the top, cramped tiny text and orphaned mini bags in the bottom corner.

A has the most coherent flow: the logo on top, the bags grouped together, then headline, copy and a prominent centred CTA. It still breaks the flavour-to-descriptor pairing, replaces three equal bags with one large and two tiny ones, and stacks the type densely. B again has a miniature CTA in the top-left corner, cramped small copy, and mini bags stranded at the bottom-left edge.
